findings.message: The `EEXIST + --push` retry path never checks that the current plan file still matches the marker's sha256, so it can publish an edited, never-approved plan to the board as the 'approved plan'. Lines 390-394: on EEXIST with `--push`, the marker is 'not re-written', Step 4b is skipped and the flow goes 'directly to Step 4c'. Step 4c then reads `.clancy/plans/{stem}.md` (line 504) and posts its content through the curl blocks. Nothing in 4a's retry branch or in 4c hashes the plan and compares it to the marker's `sha256=`, even though lines 410-412 describe that comparison as the gate. Trigger: approve plan X, the push fails, edit X.md, then run the printed retry command `/clancy:approve-plan X --push --ticket KEY`. The edited content is posted to the ticket while the marker still holds the old hash. The same branch also re-posts a duplicate comment when the earlier push succeeded, because it never checks for a prior `LOCAL_APPROVE_PLAN_PUSH` row.

The `EEXIST + --push` retry path never checks that the current plan file still hashes to the marker's `sha256=`. If the plan was edited after approval, a `--push` retry posts the edited, unapproved content to the board as 'the approved plan', and the user is never warned about the hash mismatch. Fix: before falling through to 4c, re-hash `.clancy/plans/{stem}.md` and compare it to the marker. On mismatch, refuse to push (or warn and stop) and tell the user to re-approve. Verify the approval hash before retrying a push If the plan was edited after its original approval, `--push` now publishes the current file while preserving a marker that approves different bytes. The inventory correctly treats this situation as stale, but this retry branch bypasses that distinction. Compare the current plan hash with the existing marker and require re-approval on mismatch before publishing.

The bracketed-key Source parser cannot match Notion keys (hex/UUID) or Shortcut-style keys, so Notion auto-detect never pushes and Notion Sources are wrongly classed as 'file-path'. The pushable pattern is `^\[(#?\d+|[A-Z][A-Z0-9]*-\d+)\]\s+.+$`, which allows only `#digits`, bare digits or `UPPER-digits`. Brief writes board Sources as `[{KEY}] {Title}` (brief.md:808), and Notion keys are `^[0-9a-f]{32}$|^[0-9a-f-]{36}$` (line 186 table). So `[3f2a…] Title` falls into bucket 3 ('matches anything else', line 526). That logs `BOARD_PUSH_SKIPPED_NO_TICKET | file-path` and shows 'source is file-path', which is wrong. The Notion success note added to Step 7 (line 1504) can then only fire through `--ticket`. Shortcut's `[SC-123]`, which Step 2 line 106 accepts, parses as bracketed but then hard-errors against `^\d+$`.

The bracketed-key parser only accepts `#?\d+` or `[A-Z][A-Z0-9]*-\d+`. A Notion key (32/36-char hex UUID, or the `notion-xxxxxxxx` short key that Step 2 accepts) can never be extracted, so a Notion Source always becomes 'file-path / no ticket'. Auto-detected pushes are impossible on Notion, which leaves the Notion validation row and the Notion flat-text note in Step 7 effectively unreachable without `--ticket`. Accept Notion page IDs in bracketed Source values For a Notion-backed brief, Source contains `[{page ID}] {Title}`, but the bracketed-key regex accepts only numeric or project-style keys. Consequently, a valid Notion Source is classified as a file path and skipped before reaching the Notion validator or POST block. Include the supported Notion UUID formats in Source extraction so automatic pushes work without requiring `--ticket`.

The `--ticket` override is never honoured when the plan has no Source header or has an inline-quoted or file-path Source, because those branches skip before the override is considered. This contradicts the command doc's promise that `--ticket` helps when Source is 'missing'. Line 518 says a missing `**Source:**` header makes Step 4c 'skip silently and continue to Step 7', with no `--ticket` exception. The skip-no-ticket branch (lines 530-546) logs `BOARD_PUSH_SKIPPED_NO_TICKET` and continues to Step 7, again with no exception. `--ticket` is first mentioned at line 550, after both exits. The diff's commands/approve-plan.md says `--ticket` is 'Useful when the brief Source field is missing, ambiguous'. Trigger: `/clancy:approve-plan foo --push --ticket PROJ-1` on a plan whose Source is `"Add dark mode"` follows the documented order to the skip branch, and nothing is pushed.

`--ticket` cannot rescue a missing or non-bracketed Source. A missing `**Source:**` header skips 4c silently, and inline-quoted or file-path Sources go to `BOARD_PUSH_SKIPPED_NO_TICKET`. Neither branch checks for `--ticket` first. Yet the command docs say `--ticket` is 'useful when the brief Source field is missing', and the EEXIST branch says 'Source must be readable ... or `--ticket` override must be supplied'. As written, `/clancy:approve-plan stem --push --ticket PROJ-1` on a plan with a free-text Source never pushes. The override needs to be resolved before the Source-missing and skip-no-ticket branches. `--ticket` cannot rescue a missing or non-bracketed Source. The success and failure classification depends on the HTTP status, but the duplicated curl commands never capture one. A 4xx/5xx response may be logged as a successful push. Every push block uses `curl -s` without `--fail` or `-w '%{http_code}'` (e.g. lines 638-646 and 662-668). With those options absent, curl exits 0 on HTTP 401/403/500. Yet line 742 keys success on 'When the curl returns a 2xx response' and logs `LOCAL_APPROVE_PLAN_PUSH`, and lines 760-762 require 'the literal numeric status code' for `BOARD_PUSH_FAILED`. Nothing in the commands provides that code.

Success and failure classification depend on reading the HTTP status (2xx vs 403/404/429/500), but the copied curl blocks use `curl -s` without `-w '%{http_code}'` or `--fail`. curl exits 0 on 4xx/5xx, so the status the logging contract needs is never captured. Linear's GraphQL also returns HTTP 200 with an `errors` array or `success: false`, which this contract would log as a successful push. Specify how to capture the status and check the response body, at least for Linear. Check Linear mutation results before logging push success Linear can return HTTP 200 with GraphQL `errors` or an unsuccessful `commentCreate` result. Treating every 2xx response as a live comment therefore records `LOCAL_APPROVE_PLAN_PUSH` even when nothing was posted, and omits the promised failure message and retry command. For Linear, inspect the response body and require `data.commentCreate.success` before entering this success path.

The plan body and identifiers are placed inside single-quoted `-d '...'` shell arguments. Plan text containing a `'` can break out into the shell, and `$ISSUE_ID`/`$PAGE_ID` never expand. The new `--afk --push` path reaches this sink unattended. Line 681: `-d '{"query": "mutation { commentCreate(input: { issueId: \"$ISSUE_ID\", body: \"<markdown plan>\" }) ...'`. Line 731: `-d '{"parent": {"page_id": "$PAGE_ID"}, ...}'`. Inside single quotes `$ISSUE_ID`/`$PAGE_ID` stay literal. The `<markdown plan>` content comes from the plan file, which derives from briefs and board tickets, and is interpolated with no encoding or escaping rule. Step 4c also never says how `{KEY}` maps to `$ISSUE_NUMBER` (strip `#`), `$ISSUE_ID` or `$PAGE_ID`. These blocks were copied from plan.md Step 5b, but this change adds an unattended path to them.

The `--afk`-without-`--push` decision is placed after Source parsing and key validation. An unattended run that is meant to stay local-only can therefore print a hard error and log `BOARD_PUSH_FAILED` or `BOARD_PUSH_SKIPPED_NO_TICKET` alongside or instead of `LOCAL_ONLY`. The documented order in Step 4c is: read Source (502) → parse and skip-no-ticket logging (520-546) → validate and hard-error, logging `BOARD_PUSH_FAILED | key-mismatch:{KEY}` (548-589) → decision matrix (608-627), where '`--afk` without `--push`' should 'Skip the push entirely'. No sentence moves the flag check ahead of the parse and validate sub-steps, so a mismatched Source key under plain `--afk` follows the hard-error path first.

The retry path claims auditors 'see one approval row', but Step 7 unconditionally re-renders '✅ Approved' and appends another `LOCAL_APPROVE_PLAN` row on every `--push` retry. Line 396: 'auditing tools see one approval row in `.clancy/progress.txt`, even if 4c was attempted multiple times.' Step 7 local mode (lines 1478-1516) always prints the approved block and 'Append to `.clancy/progress.txt`: ... LOCAL_APPROVE_PLAN | sha256=...' with no retry exception. Line 493's gate also still reads 'Step 4a wrote a marker successfully', which is false on the retry path.

This says 'auditing tools see one approval row in `.clancy/progress.txt`, even if 4c was attempted multiple times'. But after 4c the retry path continues to Step 7, whose local-mode block always appends `LOCAL_APPROVE_PLAN` and renders '✅ Approved {stem}'. Each retry therefore adds a duplicate approval row and a misleading success banner. Step 7 needs a retry-aware branch that skips the `LOCAL_APPROVE_PLAN` row and banner, or this claim is false. The diff rewrites an existing locked baseline test's expectation in the same change it judges. The baseline test `after writing the marker, Step 4a jumps to Step 7 (log) and skips board flow` asserted `content.toContain('jump to Step 7')`. The diff replaces it with `continues to Step 4c` assertions. The behaviour change is intended, but acceptance.md says the baseline tests are locked, and the edit carries no recorded approval.

The new tests only regex-match prose shape, and some are tautological, so they would pass with a wrong or contradictory workflow (for example, none catches the stale Step 2 'deferred' sentence or the --ticket ordering bug). 'command file --push doc references board push target' slices from the index of '`--push`' and then asserts `/push|board/i`, which the slice always matches because it begins with `--push`. 'documents the three brief Source formats' accepts `/file[- ]path|\.md/`, and `.md` appears throughout. Every Step 4c test is a `toMatch` on markdown text, and none exercises behaviour.

The Step 4c per-platform regexes don't match the Step 2 ticket-key regexes in the same file (lines 102-107). Step 2 is case-insensitive, allows a bare number for GitHub, `[A-Za-z]{1,10}-\d+` for Linear, `SC-123` for Shortcut, and the `notion-[a-f0-9]{8}` short key for Notion. Step 4c is uppercase-only, requires `#` for GitHub, and has no Shortcut prefix or Notion short-key form. A key the workflow accepts as valid in board mode will hard-error as a 'mismatch' in Step 4c, e.g. `--ticket 42` on GitHub or `--ticket proj-1` on Jira. Two divergent validation tables in one file will drift further over time. The Step 4c per-platform regexes don't match the Step 2 ticket-key regexes in the same file (lines 102-107). Step 4c never says how to derive these from the resolved `{KEY}`. Nothing tells the agent to strip `#` for GitHub. Nothing tells it to look up the Linear internal UUID from the `ENG-42` identifier, which `commentCreate.issueId` needs and which board mode gets from Step 3's query. Row ordering contradicts execution order. The `BOARD_PUSH_SKIPPED_NO_TICKET` row (and likewise `LOCAL_APPROVE_PLAN_PUSH` at line 742) is supposed to be written 'after' or 'immediately after' the `LOCAL_APPROVE_PLAN` row from Step 7. But Step 4c runs, and appends, before Step 7 writes `LOCAL_APPROVE_PLAN`. The workflow should either defer the 4c rows until Step 7 or drop the ordering claim. The command also re-supplies the key even when the failure was a key mismatch (the mismatch path prints `{CORRECT_KEY}`, but the HTTP-failure path re-prints the same key).
